_comment: The PR / push-to-main smoke selection (CI v5, docs/CI.md).
Every PR and every push to main runs ONE macOS job (ci.yml's `smoke`): it
builds once, then runs the `unit` classes below as one xcodebuild invocation
(no retry) and the `ui` classes as one invocation (one targeted retry), on
the same build and booted simulator. It answers 'does this build, and is
anything obviously broken?'. Every unit class, the timing families and the
complete UI suite run in the nightly workflow (nightly.yml, shaped by
scripts/hosted-suite.json), which also validates a release.
Rules for this list - the SIZE rule is the important one:
- ONE class per risk area (see docs/CI.md for the mapping). Every
xcodebuild invocation has a fixed hosted cost (40-100 s before its first
test, measured 2026-10-15), and the merge gate's job is a fast verdict
on a shared runner pool, not coverage: the nightly run is the exhaustive
authority. Seven unit classes is one invocation; growing the list adds
PR wall clock on every run without adding coverage the nightly lacks.
- never add the nightly-only timing families (hosted-suite.json
nightly_only_unit: TranscriptPerformanceFixtureTests,
TranscriptPerfLedgerContractTests, LongContextScalingFixtureTests,
SettledMessageIsolationTests, MarkdownRichContentHostedTests) - they
run with repeats at night and must not re-litigate on every PR;
- every name here must exist in the right target: scripts/plan-tests.py
smoke fails otherwise, so a rename cannot silently shrink PR coverage.
